name: Python for ML: Arrayo
subtitle: Run NumPy-style code on phone
shortDescription: Learn the Python behind machine learning by running it: arrays, broadcasting, gradient descent and real projects, all on your phone.
longDescription:
Learn the Python that machine learning is built on, by writing and running it on your phone.

Arrayo is a hands-on course for undergraduates and self-taught learners. Every idea starts from a real situation, you move a slider or run a few lines, and only then do you meet the equation that describes what you just saw. Nothing needs an account, a server or a connection: an interpreter for a teaching subset of Python and NumPy-style arrays runs inside the app.

NINE UNITS, BUILT UP IN ORDER
1. Python core refresher: types, loops, functions, lists and dictionaries
2. Arrays and shapes: ndarray, axes, slicing, masks, views and copies
3. Vectorisation and broadcasting: replace loops, line up shapes
4. Linear algebra in code: dot products, X @ w, matrix products, distance tables
5. Tables and data cleaning: missing values, split-apply-combine
6. Plotting and evaluation: scatter, line, bar and histogram figures, MSE and R squared
7. Reproducible experiments: seeds, splits, configs
8. From scratch: linear regression with gradient descent
9. Performance and structure: counting work, defensive checks, moving averages

HOW YOU LEARN
- Run it: every idea has a short program you can edit and run
- See it: a simulation of a real situation (grades, house prices, sensor columns, a forecaster) with sliders; tap any symbol of the equation to see what it is in the picture
- Build it: 27 coding exercises checked by running your code against real expected output, with hints and worked answers
- Four real projects: clean a sensor log, summarise and curve grades, treat a picture as an array, and predict ratings in a tiny recommender
- Labs: a slice explorer that highlights exactly which cells you picked, a broadcasting checker, a matrix product lab and a timing lab that measures loop against vector on your own device
- Checks: short, optional quizzes with a reason for every answer, computed from what you built

BUILT TO BE TRUSTED
Every expected output in the course was produced by running the same program in real CPython and NumPy, and a test suite replays hundreds of programs through both apps. Every claim lists its sources (NumPy and Python documentation, Stanford, Berkeley and CMU course pages, open textbooks and papers). Tap a source to read it in a full-width window without leaving your place. Offline, the source details are still there.

BEFORE YOU START
Arrayo teaches a subset of Python and NumPy and is not a replacement for a full installation. Random numbers come from Arrayo's own documented generator, so a seed gives the same numbers on every device. The course is original; it is not affiliated with NumPy, pandas, matplotlib or any university it cites.

Free to use. Optional ads appear only between activities, never inside an exercise or a quiz. Remove ads with a monthly subscription (7 days free), or watch a short video to earn credits.

Text size can be changed with A- and A+ at any time.
